intent: generate, then refine tone and drawing
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, a newly drawn portrait with the corrected, faithful facial likeness. Image 2 is the ORIGINAL PHOTO for identity verification only. Image 3 is the STYLE AND DARKNESS reference only. Never borrow image 3's face, hairline, proportions, age, beard, pose or clothes.

Change ONLY the tonal range and mark-making of image 1 so it belongs in the dark dry-brush ink series in image 3. Keep all of image 1's anatomy and composition EXACTLY: high forehead, hairline and irregular fine hair silhouette, broad soft cheeks, soft chin and jaw, natural hooded uneven eyes, real nose width and rounded tip, subtly asymmetric mouth, sparse moustache and chin beard, sideward gaze, head angle and round-neck shirt. The user specifically rejects idealization. No beautification, sharpened jaw, hollow cheeks, fuller luxurious hair, symmetrical model face, smaller nose or larger eyes. The exact likeness already achieved in image 1 must survive.

DARKNESS: replace the light paper-like face and very bright hair highlights with subdued NEUTRAL mid-grey planes. Brightest large planes around #777a7d, midtones around #424549, shadows near-black. In particular strongly reduce the bright top of the hair, forehead, viewer-right hair and chest. No cream, beige, sepia, brown or colour cast. The background should be dark anthracite #0d0f12 like image 3. Natural positive light/shadow, dark eyes and nostrils within grey planes, no photographic inversion or bright contour effect.

DRAWING: replace smooth photographic shading and the many tiny strands with the broad dry-brush strokes and approximately four coherent value groups of image 3. Preserve the facial contours while drawing the cheeks and forehead as larger calm areas with selective rough hatching. Keep the feature placement and shapes exact. Group the hair into irregular thin broken brush gestures; keep its naturally uneven volume, do not thicken it into a glamorous mane. Simplify beard detail without changing its sparse shape. Remove photographic grain, paper texture, detailed skin and smooth tonal blending. A few energetic rough strokes describe the clothing and outer hair; leave dark gaps and incomplete edges, with the lower torso dissolving into near-black. Clearly hand-drawn ink rather than a photographic filter, vector posterization, repeated pebble texture or glossy paint.

Same portrait, same 4:5 framing and likeness, only darker and more graphically drawn. No new objects, no text, no signature, no border.

initial_generation.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a new, faithful 1971 portrait of Jackie Leven for a dark illustrated tribute timeline.

The attached printed photograph is the ONLY visual reference. Create a fresh drawing directly from the man in this photograph, not a generic young rock musician and not a retouched or idealized version. Ignore the magazine page, headings, captions, border and background. Do not reproduce any text.

The user's specific correction is that the previous portrait was too idealized. LIKENESS AND NATURAL PROPORTIONS ARE THE HIGHEST PRIORITY. Preserve the actual face in the photograph: high broad forehead and natural exposed temples; comparatively full rounded cheeks; soft rather than sculpted jaw and chin; the exact brow thickness and asymmetry; naturally hooded, uneven eyes looking to the viewer's right; a substantial nose with the real rounded tip and width; the small natural mouth and its asymmetric corners. Keep the sparse, somewhat irregular moustache and chin beard exactly in character with the photo, not a sharply groomed designer beard. Preserve the photographed young adult age. Do not strengthen his jaw, hollow his cheeks, narrow his nose, enlarge or brighten his eyes, straighten all asymmetries, smooth everything into symmetry or make him look like a fashion model. Do not exaggerate flaws or deliberately make him unattractive either: draw this specific actual person.

His long loosely centre-parted hair is fine, irregular, slightly tangled and flyaway, with the original hairline and uneven volume. Avoid thick luxuriant waves, a perfect middle part, glamorous windblown locks or a heroic mane. Preserve the relaxed three-quarter head angle and quiet sidelong gaze from the original. Frame the head, shoulders and upper chest in a new upright 4:5 composition. Keep the original understated round-neck shirt, with only a suggestion of the surrounding outer garment translated into subdued charcoal. No invented open rock-star shirt, jewelry or props. Remove the hand/partial person at the photo edge.

Medium: visibly hand-drawn rough dry-brush ink and limited grey washes on almost-black anthracite #0d0f12, matching a subdued monochrome portrait series. Build the face from several broad, calm light/shadow planes. Use sparse precise marks to describe eyes, nose, mouth and facial hair without changing their shapes. Keep the drawing moderately abstract and raw, especially in hair, shoulders and clothing; simplify detail but never simplify away the distinctive anatomy. Irregular dry-brush gaps and broken stroke endings, with a little directional hatching. No photographic rendering, cosmetic retouching, smooth airbrushing, digital filter effect, uniform pebbly texture, glossy oil impasto, vector facets or idealized heroic lighting.

All tones strictly NEUTRAL grey, charcoal and black. No brown, sepia, cream, beige, blue or other colour tint. Subdued mid-grey facial planes, dark eyes and nostrils, natural positive lighting, no brilliant white highlights or hair halo. Background quiet and near-featureless. The outer hair and shoulders fade into darkness with unfinished brush strokes; lower chest dissolves softly. No frame, typography, signature, logo or watermark lettering.
One standalone portrait, vertical 4:5. The goal is a restrained, honest drawn likeness of the supplied photograph.
